To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the PRKCI rs546950 and PRKCI rs4955720 polymorphisms are associated with PCa susceptibility in Eastern Chinese Han population, and that the PRKCA rs546950 polymorphism is associated with PCa progression in Eastern Chinese Han patients.

the PRKCI rs4955720 and rs546950 SNPs, which were previously found to be associated with PCa in Caucasian populations, were jointly associated with a slightly decreased PCa risk in the Eastern Chinese population.
the two PRCNI polymorphisms are jointly associated with PC risk.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of PRKCI polymorphic proteins.
the role of the PRKCI polymorphism in the development of prostate cancer.
the role of the PRKCI polymorphism in the etiology and progression of prostate cancer (PC) and the possible mechanism of the PRKCA polymorphism in PCa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence of a significant association between the two PRKCA SNPs and PCa risk.
the present study is the first to evaluate the role of PRKCQ SNPs in PCa risk among Chinese populations.
there was no significant association between PRKCI polymorphism and PCa risk in Chinese men, but the two SNPs were jointly significantly associated with PCa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PRKCI SNPS rs546950 and/or rs4955720 are associated with prostate cancer in an Eastern Chinese men.
the two PRKCIs are associated with PCa in an Eastern Chinese male population.
the two PRKCIsnps rs546950 and 4955720 were jointly associated with Prostate Cancer risk in an Eastern China population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
two novel PRKCI SNPS (rs546950 and rs4995720) may contribute to prostate cancer risk in the Chinese population.
two PRKCI variants (rs546950 and rs5955270) were associated with PCa in a Chinese population and that these SNPs may be used as a marker for PCa in the Chinese population.

the two well‐designed PRKCI SNPS rs546950 and r4955720 were jointly associated with the risk of PCa in an Eastern Chinese men, and the homozygous wide‐type form for these two SNPs may be a protective factor for PCa.
